title: BOM export floods 'Unknown Items' with solid-level classification keys (multi-solid parts)
description: Server-side BOM builders (bom_excel._build_bom_data, bom_manifest.assign_bom_items / build_manifest_rows) resolve classification node_id->ref_id via _build_node_to_ref, which only maps tree leaf instance ids. Multi-solid parts classified per-solid are stored under '<ref>:s<n>' keys (frontend keys solid children by prototype ref_id). These keys aren't in node_to_ref, so each falls back to itself as a bogus ref, finds no member name and no CNC result, and lands in the Excel 'Unknown Items' sheet. Frontend _resolveClassification handles this (strips :s<n>, remaps) so the UI is correct; only the export is wrong. Repro run e8a0ba3c: 55 solid keys across 3 multi-solid parts (Main Frame, Top Support, Reinforcement) show as 55 garbage Unknown rows instead of 3 CNC items. Fix: add shared resolver that strips ':s<n>' suffix before node_to_ref lookup, used by all server BOM builders.
close_reason: Fixed: added resolve_classification_ref() in bom_manifest.py to strip ':s<n>' suffix so solid-level classification keys collapse onto their parent multi-solid ref. Wired into assign_bom_items + bom_excel._build_bom_data. Verified on run e8a0ba3c: Unknown Items 56->1, CNC Items 3->6. Regression tests in tests/test_bom_manifest.py. Follow-up cad-automation-stage2-kna for multi_solid per-solid itemisation.

title: Lightweight classification pass (decouple refined_class from NC1/DXF)
description: Circular-dependency fix: refined_class currently rides inside the heavy CNC analysis, which only runs on already-classified postprocess parts -> can't assist triage. Build a LIGHTWEIGHT classify pass that computes refined_class (features + library match + classify_part) WITHOUT generating NC1/DXF, callable on frontier refs as the user explores. Reuse the cross-section raster (already computed for holes) to derive H/W/area for the library match instead of re-slicing. Then: worker + endpoint, sidecar storage (separate 'classification' key), frontend triggers it on explode and feeds _autoClassifyFromRefinedResults. Heavy CNC analysis (NC1/DXF) stays as-is, scoped to postprocess.
notes: IMPLEMENTED (pending browser verification): lightweight classify_ref (no NC1/DXF) + classify_parts worker + POST /cnc-analysis/classify + frontend _classifyFrontier hooked on open+explode. Action-level consistency with heavy path = 100% on test set. Endpoint verified via curl. Frontier-respecting: never descends into unexploded/BO/excluded assemblies. Perf follow-up for big STEPs filed (warm-doc cache).

title: CNC/BO/Exclude routing classifier (confidence-gated ML)
description: Validated LOO test (scripts/classify_cnc_bo.py): CNC recall 99%, Exclude 94%, BO 65% (balanced acc 86%, +11% vs base). BO bulk is a make/buy decision not in geometry; grating-type BO = extreme instance_count (>=64 clean rule). Plan: auto-route confident parts, flag low-confidence (ambiguous BO) for human review. Never silently mis-route (wrong NC output).

title: Rules: plate/formed-plate/section decision-tree classifier
description: Decision tree (validated features in app/pipeline/feature_extract.py): flat plate (fill~1, t_eff~dim_thin); hollow box (n_holes>=1); open rolled section (thk_max/t_eff>1.5); uniform-open -> angle vs formed plate. Rules beat ML here (crisp physics, few labels). Emit per-branch confidence; flag low-confidence for review. Wire into cnc_shape_analyser as the plate/section gate once validated.
notes:
Decision tree validated at 92.1% (266 labels): holes>=1->SECTION;
t_eff_thin_ratio>=0.45->PLATE; rule_type==section->SECTION; thk_max_over_teff>=1.5
->SECTION; else FORMED_PLATE. Logic lives in collate_candidates.predict() + 
scripts/eval_rules.py. STILL TODO: port into a real classifier module and wire
into cnc_shape_analyser as the plate/section gate (with confidence + low-conf flag).
Residual error is the unmatched angle-vs-formed boundary -> needs rw7.2 bend-radius.
Decision tree now 4 classes at 91.9% (eval_rules.py): nbends>=5->BENT_SECTION; holes>=1->SECTION; t_thin>=0.45->PLATE; nbends>=1->FORMED_PLATE; rule_type==section->SECTION; thk>=1.5->SECTION; else FORMED_PLATE.
Follow-on: refined_class now auto-applies the manual classification (postprocess/bought-out/exclude) for unclassified parts at >=0.5 confidence, leaving low-conf/MIXED flagged for review (analysis.js _autoClassifyFromRefinedResults). This is the labour-saving integration — the BOM columns are just the audit trail (review happens before BOM).
close_reason: Done: classify_part() (app/pipeline/part_classifier.py) is the single source of truth (91.4% on 616 labels). Wired into the live STEP pipeline (cnc_shape_analyser._analyse_single attaches refined_class/confidence/reason; multi-solid gets an aggregate). Surfaced in the BOM Excel (CNC/Unknown sheets: Refined Class/Conf/Review cols) and the frontend analysis badge. Validated end-to-end (Portal Assembly BOM 7/7). Base type/routing unchanged. IFC stream left untouched (metadata-only, no geometric classification) per design.

title: Automated part classification (plate/formed/section + CNC/BO routing)
description: Two automation tracks discovered 2026-06-08/09. (1) Geometric subtype plate/formed-plate/section via explainable RULES. (2) CNC/Bought-out/Exclude routing via confidence-gated ML using the user's existing classifications as labels. Foundation built: feature_extract.py (incl. cross-section raster: holes/thickness), feature_export.py (dataset + aligned cnc_class), labelling gallery, eval scripts (train_designation.py, classify_cnc_bo.py).

title: AR Phase 0: pose-solve + CAD-edge projection core (single-section alignment spike)
description: First buildable AR step. Prove CAD aligns to a photo: given a calibration profile + 2D-3D correspondences, solvePnP -> camera pose -> project the section's CAD edges to 2D overlay polylines. Verify on a single uploaded section (no welds; tests pose/overlay only). Increment 1 = backend pose+projection core (app/services/pose.py) verified headlessly with synthetic section. Increment 2 = OCC CAD-edge extraction in world coords from an analysed part. Increment 3 = Capture tab UI (manual-correspondence click -> overlay), local storage (outputs/captures/), under a new PRODUCTION nav group. Storage: Supabase table + Storage bucket later (not the ISO doc service); formal ratification report -> doc service later. Design in vault AR-weld-ratification-tool.md.
notes: ALL 3 increments built + verified headlessly (32 tests pass; solve recovers pose 0.0mm/0.0px; capture stores provenance). Capture tab live under PRODUCTION nav. PENDING: live browser test — overlay CAD edges on a REAL photo of section feac0770. Photo MUST be 6048x6048 (Stephano Iphone calibration res) or the gate blocks Solve.
close_reason: PROVEN end-to-end on real data: CAD edges of section feac0770 overlaid correctly onto a real iPhone photo via manual-correspondence pose (6 points). Calibration -> world-coord geometry -> solvePnP (SQPNP) -> projection chain all confirmed. Capture tab live. Next: marker-based auto-registration (remove manual clicking); then welds on a real weldment.

title: Camera calibration UI (ChArUco) for AR weld-ratification tool
description: Add a 'Calibrate' tab to the frontend that captures ChArUco board views (live webcam via getUserMedia + image upload) and computes camera intrinsics server-side with OpenCV. Saves named camera profiles to outputs/calibration/ for the upcoming AR overlay tool. First concrete step toward the AR weld-ratification tool (see vault note projects/cad-automation/AR-weld-ratification-tool.md). Adds opencv-contrib-python-headless to requirements (needs docker rebuild).
notes: Implemented + verified backend end-to-end in container (opencv-contrib 4.10, ChArUco detect/compute/profiles all pass via HTTP). Frontend page wired (Calibrate tab), JS validates as ESM, static served 200. REMAINING: live in-browser getUserMedia webcam path needs manual test in a browser (can't drive headlessly). Not yet committed/pushed.
close_reason: Delivered + verified end-to-end with real iPhone photos: 12/12 views detect (AprilTag), healthy intrinsics, profile saved. Board config now persists. Note: live getUserMedia webcam capture path not yet exercised (upload path fully proven) — raise a new issue if a webcam user hits problems.

title: Warm-doc cache for frontier classify (big-STEP perf)
description: The /cnc-analysis/classify endpoint opens the STEP via _read_xcaf per call (per explode). For large STEP files (~97MB ~27s parse) that makes each explode sluggish. Options: keep a warm parsed XCAF doc server-side (persistent classify worker / in-proc cache), or precompute lightweight refined_class for all leaves once after consolidation (cheap, no NC1/DXF) and have the frontend just read it. Small/medium jobs are fine today.

title: EXCLUDE/artifact detector (stop artifacts polluting formed bucket)
description: 40 labelled EXCLUDE artifacts (filled-in holes, broken/degenerate geometry) currently fall through to the 'formed' else-branch, dragging FORMED_PLATE precision to 33%. Find their geometric signature and add an EXCLUDE rule ahead of the geometric tree. Improves overall reliability.
close_reason: Done: volume_mm3<10000 -> EXCLUDE rule (eval_rules.py + gallery). 82% artifact recall, 92% precision, 0 false-excludes on 616 labels. Lifted SECTION/PLATE precision to 98/99%. Remaining 18% are larger artifacts (>10k mm3).

title: Known catalogue-product BO detection (Unistrut, etc.)
description: Some bought-out items ARE confidently identifiable (unlike the general make/buy call). Unistrut = proprietary strut-channel (channel w/ inturned rolled lips), always BO, identifiable by name ('SUPP UNIST...') and by its distinctive cross-section. Build a small extensible 'known catalogue products' list mapping name/shape -> BOUGHT_OUT. CAVEAT: name match must be specific -- 'SUPP UNIST PLATE 2mm' is a CNC plate, not strut (rule: contains 'unist' AND NOT 'plate'). Start with name rules; add the rolled-lip channel shape detector for unnamed cases. Only 6 parts/3 names in current corpus but the pattern generalises.
notes:
REOPENED: name-based rule alone is insufficient — part name is NOT guaranteed
(Steve, 2026-06-09). Name rule (catalogue_products.py) stays as a high-confidence
shortcut, but need SHAPE-based Unistrut detection for unnamed parts:
signature = thin uniform wall (low t_eff) + open channel envelope (~41mm squarish)
+ inturned ROLLED LIPS (convex bends near the opening -> n_convex_bends>0) making
the section nearly-closed (slot, not full hole). Approach: cross-section template
/ signature match on the raster + bend faces. Until then Unistrut without the name
falls through to the geometric tree (likely mislabelled formed/section).

title: Bent section class + detector (in-house section/tube bending)
description: Gap found 2026-06-09 reviewing gallery: a bent CHS handrail (curved tube, multiple bends) is made in-house but fits none of plate/formed-plate/straight-section/BO. It's a 5th class: BENT_SECTION, manufacturing route = section/tube bending. Signature: constant tube profile but curved/multi-bend centreline -> centreline_length (=volume/CSA) >> dim_long; slice perpendicular to bbox-long-axis is not a clean constant profile. Added 'Bent section' to the labelling gallery (collate_candidates.py). TODO: detection feature (centreline-to-envelope ratio / non-straight sweep) in feature_extract.py; add to decision tree + CNC sub-routing (cut / brake-bend / saw-drill / section-bend).
notes: Bent-section DETECTION is working via n_convex_bends>=5 (100% recall, 58% precision on labelled set) -- delivered by rw7.2. Remaining: improve precision + the centreline/envelope feature for tessellated curved members; wire BENT_SECTION into the routing.

title: Label 300-part gallery; tune + validate rule classifier
description: Gallery at /outputs/stl/_formed_candidates/gallery.html (300 distinct geoms, 40 jobs, holes/thickness shown). User classifies section/plate/formed/bought-out; Export CSV -> app/pipeline/data/labels/verified.csv. 29 already labelled (9 formed, 6 section, 14 plate). Use to tune thresholds + measure rule accuracy.
close_reason: Done: ~290 parts labelled across 40 jobs (all 6 classes) -> verified.csv. Rule decision tree calibrated to 92.1% on the 266 geometric labels (SECTION 92% / PLATE 98% recall) via scripts/eval_rules.py. Gallery live-preview uses the same tree.

title: Bend-radius feature: rolled angle vs formed plate
description: The one geometric distinction left: rolled angle = sharp outer 90deg corner; formed plate = rounded outer bend (R>=gauge), arbitrary angle. Detect via convex cylindrical face parallel to extrusion (BRep face-type) or outer-corner radius in the cross-section raster. Add to feature_extract.py; validate against gallery labels.
close_reason: Done: n_convex_bends feature in feature_extract.py (convex cylinder, R/t_eff>=0.9, 30-270deg arc; excludes holes + rolled toes). Decision tree -> 91.9% on 4 geometric classes (273 labels). Rescues 43% of formed plates (~5% FP) and detects bent sections at 100% recall (>=5 bends).

title: AR capture pipeline: ML-ready data schema (BOP-aligned) + provenance/quality logging
description: Bake ML-readiness into the AR capture pipeline from Phase 0/1 (not bolted on later). Every capture = a permanent, fully-described training record. Persist per photo: original full-res image (no recompress, EXIF), exact intrinsics (calibration profile), solved 6DoF pose (label), CAD run_id, camera/lens/zoom + lock state; pose label QUALITY (per-marker reprojection error/confidence); marker pixel regions (for masking so the model can't cheat); adopt BOP dataset format; auto-derive masks + dense image->CAD-surface correspondences by rendering CAD at solved pose; store verification outcomes (discrepancy flags/sign-offs tied to weld ID+image) as a second dataset; log free device extras (ARKit pose, gravity, LiDAR depth); compute/store CAD symmetries + as-designed CAD snapshot; bias capture toward angle/lighting diversity. Rationale + full spec in vault note projects/cad-automation/AR-weld-ratification-tool.md (ML-readiness section). Items 1-3 (provenance, label quality, marker masks) are load-bearing and ~free to add now.

title: AR weld-ratification: Phase 0 projection spike + registration design
description: Next step after the shipped camera-calibration UI (eop). Prove the intrinsics->pose->projection chain: one photo, one marker, one weld cluster, overlay weld polylines from /connections/result/{f} onto a real photo via solvePnP. Then build out the registration design developed 2026-06-11 (see vault note projects/cad-automation/AR-weld-ratification-tool.md): marker constellation, CAD-driven marker placement planner (OBB + faces + weld clusters + classification -> marker plan + bill of markers), feature-based pose refinement (donut/hole-concentric + corner/edge markers; targeted signature search doubles as ratification), magnetic rigid marker kit with standoff offset + unique IDs. Spike ONE region first. Design only so far; no AR code written.

title: Excel BOM: itemise multi_solid CNC parts into per-solid rows
description: bom_excel._write_cnc_sheet writes one row per BOM item using top-level cnc.mass_kg/dims, which are None for multi_solid results (per-solid data lives in solids[]). So multi-solid weldments (e.g. Main Frame on run e8a0ba3c) render as a single row with blank dims/mass and contribute 0 to CNC total weight in the Summary sheet. Pre-existing for any multi-solid part, surfaced by cad-automation-stage2-s10. Fix: expand multi_solid results into one row per solid (mirror bom_builder._rows_for_instance), or aggregate mass across solids for the single row + show solid count. Affects Summary weight totals too.

title: Designation ID ground-truth gap
description: Fine-grained section designation ML blocked by labels: corpus part-names are CAM marks, not Tekla designations (classify_by_name matches ~0). Only ~2% carry verbose ISO/DIN/BS designations (noisy). Options: extend name parser for 'STD - SIZE - LENGTH' format; or manual verification. Library-NN designation matching is the fallback.

title: Recover bought-out training labels
description: BO under-represented (only ~196 distinct shapes with geometry). ~47% of BO labels (N1092 jobs) have NO STEP upload -> re-upload to recover. C25001 BO is mostly one grating-bar geometry x2000 instances (dedups to ~158). More balanced BO data would lift the 65% recall ceiling.
